{{Elections in Virginia}}
The '''2026 United States Senate election in Virginia''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the [[Commonwealth of Virginia]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Mark Warner]] is seeking a fourth term. He is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Army general [[Bert Mizusawa]].

In the August 4 [[primary elections]], Warner was unopposed for the Democratic nomination. Mizusawa won the Republican nomination with 51.5% of the vote over Marine Corps Reserves officer David Williams and financial accountant Kim Farington.

Republicans have not won a Senate election in Virginia since [[2002 United States Senate election in Virginia|2002]].

== General election ==
===Campaign===
Two proposed debates were canceled, with the Warner campaign's noncommittal stance cited as the reason for both cancellations. On September 8, [[AARP]] announced that "The People's Debate," scheduled for October 7 in [[Richmond, Virginia|Richmond]], had been canceled.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Beyer|first1=Elizabeth|title=Warner and Mizusawa may not debate in 2026 Senate race|url=https://cardinalnews.org/2026/09/10/warner-and-mizusawa-may-not-debate-in-2026-senate-race/|date=September 10, 2026|access-date=September 23, 2026|website=Cardinal news}}</ref> A week later, on September 15, the [[League of Women Voters]] also announced the cancellation of its proposed debate planned for the first week of October.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Englander|first1=Tyler|title=Another Virginia Senate debate canceled, then things get complicated|url=https://www.wric.com/news/politics/capitol-connection/va-senate-debate-canceled-warner-mizusawa/|date=September 15, 2026|access-date=September 23, 2026|website=[[WRIC-TV]]}}</ref>
